newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Jan 97 natgas output 4.3 bln cfd -Pemex.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Jan 97 natgas output 4.3 bln cfd -Pemex.

text.p: Mexico's natural gas output in January was 4.3 billion cubic feet per day (cfd), the chairman of state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexican (Pemex) said Friday in a private meeting with U.S. and Canadian investors.
January's output compares to production of 4.18 billion cfd in the year-ago period, according to Pemex figures.
Adrian Lajous said natural gas output should "grow vigorously" through the end of the decade and that domestic consumption should also rise.
Pemex has forecast average 1997 natural gas production of 4.5 billion cfd, a 25 percent increase from the volume produced in 1994.

"Pemex Gas is deploying a major effort in order to recover and expand its gas processing capacity, optimize its systems and revamp its facilities," Lajous said, according to a transcript of his remarks issued by Pemex.

He outlined the company's 1997 production projects, specifically for Mexico's largest non-associated gas basin, Burgos Basin near the Rio Grande fields in Texas. Private exploration and field development bids will be accepted through March 14 and the contract awarded on April 22, Lajous said.
